medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all IHD patients (first_line).

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and ARB increase risk of hyperkalaemia, acute kidney injury and hypotension.
Additive blood pressure and heart‑rate lowering; may cause symptomatic hypotension.
interactions_checked.action: Titrate doses gradually; monitor BP and HR after each change.

interactions_checked.interaction: Beta‑blockers can mask hypoglycaemia symptoms, increasing risk of unrecognised hypoglycaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood glucose closely after insulin dose reduction; educate patient on hypoglycaemia signs.

interactions_checked.interaction: Dual antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk.
interactions_checked.action: Assess bleeding risk; consider proton‑pump inhibitor gastro‑protection.

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for electrolyte disturbances (potassium loss vs retention).
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and renal function after any dose change.

contraindications.reason: Duplicate RAAS blockade with lisinopril (ACE‑I) – contraindicated per NICE.
Would be combined with beta‑blocker, risking heart block and asystole (NICE contraindication).
If nitrate therapy is added, concomitant sildenafil can cause severe hypotension (NICE contraindication).

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; assumed >30 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 1.6 mg/dL and age 51, allowing ACE‑I use but renal function will be monitored.
Baseline liver function tests not available; will obtain before up‑titrating atorvastatin to 80 mg.
Time since NSTEMI not documented; dual antiplatelet therapy (prasugrel) is continued assuming patient is within the 12‑month window.
No documented allergy history; monitor for hypersensitivity to aspirin, statin, ACE‑I.
Anemia present; aspirin may increase bleeding risk – monitor haemoglobin.
HbA1c 3.0 % and random glucose 68 mg/dL indicate probable insulin overtreatment; insulin regimen will be reviewed urgently.
treatment_summary: The plan aligns the patient’s regimen with NICE CG126/NG185: continue lifelong aspirin and prasugrel (if within 12 months post‑ACS), upgrade to high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg, optimise lisinopril and bisoprolol doses, increase amlodipine to 5 mg, discontinue losartan to avoid duplicate RAAS blockade, and adjust insulin to prevent hypoglycaemia. Add isosorbide mononitrate only if angina remains uncontrolled. Monitoring includes renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, BP/HR, glucose, and haemoglobin, with lifestyle advice and cardiac rehabilitation referral.
